name: Tessera Industries Optical Fiber Tap Detector OFT-1
product_name: Tessera Industries Optical Fiber Tap Detector OFT-1
description: A diagnostic tool that detects unauthorized taps on fiber-optic cables by measuring signal loss at micro-dB resolution — far more sensitive than standard network monitoring equipment. The OFT-1 sends a calibrated light pulse through a fiber and measures the return signal with precision that can identify the 0.1 dB loss caused by a micro-bend optical tap. The device maps the location of any detected tap to within 10 cm along the fiber run, allowing physical identification and removal. Tessera developed it as a counter to their own OT-1 optical tap — and sells both the attack and the defense.

specifications.output: Fiber loss map with anomaly flags

story_hooks: An OFT-1 sweep of a corporate network found 23 unauthorized optical taps across the facility — some had been in place for over two years, and the combined data loss is measured in petabytes.

A Tessera OFT-1 has been found to have a firmware modification that causes it to report clean results on fibers that actually have taps — the counter-surveillance tool has been sabotaged to protect existing surveillance.
related_entities: Tessera Industries Optical Tap Micro-Splice OT-1

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact handheld diagnostic unit with a wedge-shaped profile — tapered from a thick control end to a slender probe tip. The design suggests precision instrumentation: clean angles, minimal ornamentation. Two prominent fiber-optic connector ports occupy the narrow end, flanked by status indicators. Overall impression is industrial and purposeful.
physical_description.dimensions: 18 cm length, 7 cm width at widest (control section), 4 cm depth. Pocket-sized to backpack-portable.
physical_description.weight_description: 500 grams — handheld with ergonomic grip. Light enough for sustained fieldwork, substantial enough to suggest quality engineering.
physical_description.primary_material: Anodized aerospace-grade aluminum chassis with reinforced polymer grip panels
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal with micro-textured grip surfaces. Chassis edges beveled and polished. Connector end polished to high gloss to minimize dust.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray body with black grip panels. Accent lights: amber for active scan, red for anomaly detection, blue for standby. Stainless steel probe tip with faint iridescent oil-film from precision machining.
physical_description.interface_elements: Two SC/APC fiber-optic connectors at probe end. 2.4-inch monochrome LCD display (320x240) with blue-tinted matrix readout. Five tactile buttons arranged in cross pattern below display: SCAN, LOCATE, MAP, RESET, MENU. USB-C charging port on right side. 3.5mm jack for auxiliary telemetry output.
distinctive_features: Micro-precision fiber connectors with dust caps tethered by kevlar cord
Real-time waveform graph scrolling continuously across LCD — shows fiber signal strength topology
Tessera Industries logo embossed in lower right, overlaid with Vasquez Biocompatible Materials copyright stamp
Small circular window above left connector showing fiber coupling lens — visible as faint blue-tinted optics beneath strengthened glass
Subtle horizontal ridges across grip panels for tactile feedback during precision manipulation
Battery status bar integrated into LCD frame — depletes visually as charge drains
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Tessera Industries logo (interlocking tessellated squares in serif typeface). Vasquez Biocompatible Materials name stamped on back. Model designation OFT-1 laser-etched below display. Regulatory compliance marks: GLMZ-certified, UL equivalent mark, recycling symbol.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn units show micro-scratches on aluminum chassis. Connector ends frequently wrapped in protective silicone dust covers. Display may have faint burn-in of grid patterns from extended use. Grip panels sometimes replaced with aftermarket rubberized overlays for better handling in cold environments. Unit often paired with external telemetry recorder clipped to user harness.
